gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Notebookcheck measured the Minisforum N5 Pro (Ryzen AI 9 HX PRO 370, 12C/24T) idling at 11.8–15.9 W. That is below the drive-less UGREEN DXP6800 Pro (up to 22.4 W, Notebookcheck), the Minisforum MS-01 (25–29 W, ServeTheHome) and the MS-A2 (25 W, ServeTheHome), so the strongest VM box in the lineup also measured lowest at idle.
standout_why: I read five rival pages. homelabpicks.com (2026-03-15) states it did no testing and lists only vendor power ratings for its picks: TerraMaster F4-424 Pro, QNAP TS-464 and Asustor AS5402T. computingforgeeks.com (2026-10-21) gives fio NFS vs iSCSI figures from a nested Proxmox lab but no power figure and no per-product hardware measurement. ITPro (2024-04-29) and StorageReview (2024-04-19) on the DXP6800 Pro report no wattage; StorageReview gives CIFS throughput and IOPS and says VMs were 'coming soon'. The one measured power figure in ChatGPT's results is Notebookcheck's DXP6800 Pro review (rank 10, not cited). It covers that one model only. No result measures the N5 Pro, MS-01, MS-A2, DXP4800 Plus or AS6804T, and none puts the boxes side by side.
decides: For a box running Proxmox around the clock, idle draw is the running cost. The N5 Pro has the most CPU of the candidates (Notebookcheck: Cinebench R23 multi 21,474) and still measured the lowest drive-less idle, so the extra cores cost nothing at idle. That backs the N5 Pro over the DXP6800 Pro for a VM-heavy all-in-one. The MS-01 and MS-A2 idle at 25 W or more with no hard drives at all, which weakens the 'separate mini PC plus NAS' route ChatGPT suggested: a second box for the drives adds its own draw on top. Each lab used its own setup, so treat these as rough ranges. They are not a single controlled test.
